# Erdős Problem 476

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/476](https://www.erdosproblems.com/476)
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.

- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.

  derivatives and additive theory*. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1994), 140-146.
-/

namespace Erdos476

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$. Let
$$
A\hat{+}A = \{ a+b : a\neq b \in A\}.
$$
Is it true that
$$
\lvert A\hat{+}A\rvert \geq \min(2\lvert A\rvert-3,p)?
$$

This is the Erdős-Heilbronn inequality, proved by Dias da Silva and Hamidoune.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos476.lean"]
theorem erdos_476 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, Fact p.Prime → ∀ A : Finset (ZMod p),
      A.restrictedSumset.card ≥ min (2 * A.card - 3) p := by
  sorry

end Erdos476

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement uses Finset (ZMod p) and truncated natural-number subtraction in min (2 * A.card - 3) p, whereas the source uses subsets of the prime field and ordinary subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For prime p, ZMod p is the p-element field, so every subset is represented by a finset. The shared restrictedSumset definition has exactly the source's membership condition: a sum of two unequal elements of A, counted without multiplicity. For |A| ≥ 2, natural and integer subtraction agree. For |A| = 0 or 1, the integer lower bounds are negative while the natural lower bound is zero; both inequalities hold automatically because the sumset cardinality is nonnegative. Review476.full_source_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves the complete equivalence with the set-based, integer-bound statement without sorry.
